arxiv-1704-00982.title: Angular changes of complex Fourier coefficients of cusp forms
arxiv-1704-00982.creator: Mohammed Amin Amri
arxiv-1704-00982.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the “angular changes” behavior of some subfamilies of Fourier coefficients of both integral and half-integral weight holomorphic cusp forms, thus one gets information about signs of the real an imaginary parts of these subfamilies. These give an extension of some recent results of Kohnen and his collaborators.

arxiv-1712-00455.title: Self-Destructing Dark Matter Preprint: FERMILAB-PUB-17-505-T
arxiv-1712-00455.creator: Yuval Grossman, Roni Harnik, Ofri Telem, Yue Zhang
arxiv-1712-00455.description: Abstract We present Self-Destructing Dark Matter (SDDM), a new class of dark matter models which are detectable in large neutrino detectors. In this class of models, a component of dark matter can transition from a long-lived state to a short-lived one by scattering off of a nucleus or an electron in the Earth.

arxiv-2105-08225.title: On r r -dynamic coloring on lexicographic product of star graphs
arxiv-2105-08225.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by . In this research, the exact results on r r -dynamic coloring of lexicographic product of path with star graph, path with double star graph, path with triple star graph and finally complete graph with path are obtained.

arxiv-2108-09155.title: Spherical objects and stability conditions on 2-Calabi–Yau quiver categories
arxiv-2108-09155.creator: Asilata Bapat and Anand Deopurkar and Anthony M. Licata
arxiv-2108-09155.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Asilata Bapat and Anand Deopurkar and Anthony M. Licata. Consider a 2-Calabi–Yau triangulated category with a Bridgeland stability condition. We devise an effective procedure to reduce the phase spread of an object by applying spherical twists. Using this, we give new proofs of the following theorems for 2-Calabi–Yau categories associated to ADE quivers: (1) all spherical objects lie in a single orbit of the braid group, and (2) the space of Bridgeland stability conditions is connected.

arxiv-2511-12012.title: Arbitrary High Order Low-rank Completely Positive and Trace Preserving (CPTP) Schemes for Lindblad Equations with Time-dependent Hamiltonian
arxiv-2511-12012.creator: Jiuhua Hu, Daniel Appelö, Yingda Cheng
arxiv-2511-12012.description: Abstract Abstract In this paper, we develop a framework for designing arbitrary high order low-rank schemes for the Lindblad equation with time-dependent Hamiltonians. Our approach is based on nested Picard iterative integrators (NPI) and results in schemes in Kraus form that are completely positive and trace preserving (CPTP).

Recently, it has become apparent that CLDN gene expression is frequently altered in several human cancers. However, the exact patterns of CLDN expression in variou

lucian-works-fowler-vol-1.title: The Works of Lucian of Samosata, Vol. I
lucian-works-fowler-vol-1.creator: Lucian of Samosata (H. W. Fowler and F. G. Fowler, trans.)
lucian-works-fowler-vol-1.description: Vol. I of the Fowler brothers' complete Lucian — including the 'Lover of Lies' (Philopseudes) with its sorcerer's-apprentice tale and 'Alexander the False Prophet', antiquity's sharpest satires of magicians and superstition.

pmc-10485129.title: Adjusting the range of cell–cell communication enables fine-tuning of cell fate patterns from checkerboard to engulfing
pmc-10485129.creator: Simon Schardt, Sabine C Fischer
pmc-10485129.description: During development, spatio-temporal patterns ranging from checkerboard to engulfing occur with precise proportions of the respective cell fates. Key developmental regulators are intracellular transcriptional interactions and intercellular signaling. We present an analytically tractable mathematical model based on signaling that reliably generates different cell type patterns with specified proportions.

pmc-10520286.title: Primary mucinous carcinoma of the skin
pmc-10520286.creator: Takayuki Yamada
pmc-10520286.description: Key Clinical MessageMucinous carcinoma of the skin is clinically characterized by good mobility, slow growth, a macroscopically smooth surface, no easy contact bleeding, and no internal flow on color Doppler; it is thus difficult to distinguish from benign tumors.AbstractA 58‐year‐old man presented to our clinic complaining of a right cheek induration, growing over the previous 6 months.

pmc-10647789.title: Role of the Autism Risk Gene Shank3 in the Development of Atherosclerosis: Insights from Big Data and Mechanistic Analyses
pmc-10647789.creator: Hsiu-Wen Chang, Ming-Jen Hsu, Li-Nien Chien, Nai-Fang Chi, Meng-Chieh Yu, Hsiu-Chen Chen, Yuan-Feng Lin, Chaur-Jong Hu
pmc-10647789.description: Increased medical attention is needed as the prevalence of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) rises. Both cardiovascular disorder (CVD) and hyperlipidemia are closely associated with adult ASD. Shank3 plays a key genetic role in ASD. We hypothesized that Shank3 contributes to CVD development in young adults with ASD. In this study, we investigated whether Shank3 facilitates the development of atherosclerosis.

pmc-10736588.title: AGE DIFFERENCES IN PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS AFTER MULTIPLE DISASTER EXPOSURES: EFFECT OF NEGATIVE COVID-19 IMPACTS
pmc-10736588.creator: Zhirui Chen, Zhen Cong
pmc-10736588.description: This study examined how older adults differed from their younger counterparts in psychological distress following exposures to tornadoes and the COVID-19 pandemic; and how the multidimensional negative COVID-19 impacts contextualized the above age differences. Data used were from a two-wave panel study of tornado victims during the COVID-19 pandemic (N = 554).

pmc-11360245.title: Immunogenicity and Safety of SARS-CoV-2 Protein Subunit Recombinant Vaccine (IndoVac®) as a Heterologous Booster Dose against COVID-19 in Indonesian Adolescents
pmc-11360245.creator: Eddy Fadlyana, Kusnandi Rusmil, Muhammad Gilang Dwi Putra, Frizka Primadewi Fulendry, Nitta Kurniati Somantri, Alvira Dwilestarie Putri, Rini Mulia Sari, Mita Puspita, Gianita Puspita Dewi, Ralph A Tripp
pmc-11360245.description: Adolescents are vulnerable to Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) infections; thus, their antibodies should be maintained above the protective value. This study aimed to evaluate the immune response and safety to the SARS-CoV-2 protein subunit recombinant vaccine (IndoVac®) as a heterologous booster dose against COVID-19 in Indonesian adolescents.

pmc-11396107.title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance for Structural Aortic Valve Stenosis Procedures
pmc-11396107.creator: Marcos Ferrández-Escarabajal, Michael Hadley, Javier Sanz, Gian Luigi Nicolosi
pmc-11396107.description: The number of structural aortic valve procedures has increased significantly in recent years. Pre-procedural planning and follow-up with noninvasive testing are essential. Although cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is the gold standard for assessing left ventricular mass, volume, and function, it is not performed routinely in patients undergoing structural interventions.

pmc-11588982.title: Embedding equity and inclusion in universities through motivational theory and community‐based conservation approaches
pmc-11588982.creator: Maï Yasué, Netta Weinstein, Sara E. Harris, I‐Chant A. Chiang, Nicole Legate, Ashley J. Moore, Nadia Joe
pmc-11588982.description: Despite widespread plans to embed justice, equity, decolonization, indigenization, and inclusion (JEDII) into universities, progress toward deeper, systemic change is slow. Given that many community‐based conservation (CBC) scholars have experience creating enduring social change in diverse communities, they have transferable skills that could help embed JEDII in universities.

pmc-11606516.title: Dysregulating mTORC1-4E-BP2 signaling in GABAergic interneurons impairs hippocampus-dependent learning and memory
pmc-11606516.creator: Ziying Huang, Shane Wiebe, Anmol Nagpal, Junghyun Choi, Caleb Walters, Niaz Mahmood, Arkady Khoutorsky, Jean-Claude Lacaille, Nahum Sonenberg
pmc-11606516.description: Memory formation is contingent on molecular and structural changes in neurons in response to learning stimuli—a process known as neuronal plasticity. The initiation step of mRNA translation is a gatekeeper of long-term memory by controlling the production of plasticity-related proteins in the brain.

pmc-11677956.title: Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Atrial Flutter and Oral Anticoagulation: The Predictive Role of Left Atrial Appendage Thrombus in a Long-Term, Prospective, Observational Cohort Study
pmc-11677956.creator: Łukasz Turek, Marcin Sadowski, Jacek Kurzawski, Marianna Janion, Boyoung Joung
pmc-11677956.description: Background/Objectives: The risks of blood clot formation, stroke, heart failure (HF), and cardiovascular death are enhanced in individuals with atrial flutter (AFL). However, it remains unclear whether left atrial appendage thrombus (LAAT) in individuals with AFL with anticoagulation enhances the risk of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.

pmc-12470206.title: Development and Validity Evaluation of the Index of Social Work Process in Promoting Social Participation of Welfare Recipients (SWP-PSP) in Japan
pmc-12470206.creator: Yukiko Takagi, Hideki Hashimoto, Albert Nienhaus
pmc-12470206.description: Social workers are required to have the capacity to effectively support welfare recipients to restore their labor participation for social inclusion. However, a systematic method for process evaluation of this capacity has not yet been established. In this study, we developed the Index of Social Work Process in Promoting Social Participation of Welfare Recipients (SWP-PSP) to address this gap.

pmc-12998261.title: Serial section videography (SSV): A low‐cost protocol for generating 3D reconstructions of internal plant structure
pmc-12998261.creator: Jacob S Suissa, Giselle Reyes
pmc-12998261.description: PremiseAnalyzing structural changes along the length of an organ provides insight into its development. However, traditional histological methods are limited by intensive procedures and size restrictions. Micro‐computed tomography (microCT) enables non‐destructive internal imaging along the length of an organ, but high cost, technical complexity, and limited accessibility hinder widespread application.

pmc-13113650.title: Unravelling Multilayered RNA Modification Networks in Female Reproduction and Obstetric/Gynaecologic Disorders
pmc-13113650.creator: Yujie Kuai, Yanjun Yi, Xinyu Li, Zhuangping Wang, Yan Zheng, Yuxuan Li, Yulin Li
pmc-13113650.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objective: RNA modifications, including N6-methyladenosine (m6A), 5-methylcytosine (m5C), 7-methylguanosine (m7G), N1-methyladenosine (m1A), pseudouridine (Ψ), N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C), 5-methoxycarbonylmethyl-2-thiouridine (mcm5s2U) and adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) editing, constitute a critical layer of post-transcriptional regulation that influences RNA stability, splicing, translation and degradation. This review aims to systematically summarise the current understanding of the molecular mechanisms and regulatory networks of RNA modifications in the female reproductive physiology and to evaluate their pathological implications in obstetric and gynaecologic disorders.

pmc-13251172.title: Reduced peripheral natural killer cell counts may be a predictive marker for cesarean scar pregnancy
pmc-13251172.creator: Ye Shen, Jinqiu Zhang, Hua Fang, Li Zhang, Qi Jiang, Hua Gong, Qi Chen, Min Zhao
pmc-13251172.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP), a condition characterised by inflammation, occurs in 0.2% of women with a history of cesarean section(s), and is clinically categorised by type 1 and type 2 according to the ultrasound findings. Recent studies reported that systemic inflammation indices derived from routine whole-blood tests may serve as additional clinical predictive markers for early CSP detection, with lymphocyte counts showing a reduction. However, the specific lymphocyte populations contributing to this reduction remain unclear.

pmc-13422752.title: Detection of Antibiotic‐Resistant Campylobacter on Retail Chicken in New Zealand: A Sentinel Survey
pmc-13422752.creator: Kathleen J. Sircombe, Daniel Pletzer, Sarah Hook

pmc-13524146.title: Educational Utility of a Full-Skull 3-Dimensional Model for Skull Base Surgery Training
pmc-13524146.creator: Daisuke Kuga, Koji Yoshimoto
pmc-13524146.description: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES:Skull base surgery requires precise 3-dimensional (3D) anatomic understanding and advanced drilling techniques within a confined operative space. Although cadaveric dissection remains the gold standard for training, its availability is limited. This study aimed to evaluate the educational utility of a commercially available full-skull 3D model for skull base surgery training.

pmc-13619208.title: Factors associated with occult acute rib fractures on chest CT after negative radiography in older fall patients
pmc-13619208.creator: Joo Han Kwon, Won Young Sung
pmc-13619208.description: In older patients with fall-related injuries, chest computed tomography (CT) can detect acute rib fractures after chest radiography (CXR) showed no evidence of acute fracture. We evaluated clinical factors associated with CT-reported acute rib fracture within this clinician-selected imaging pathway.
